title: Compactness of a closed complex polydisc and its product with a compact set
statement:
Use $\mathbf C$ with its usual absolute value and topology [def-weil-field]. Let $d\geq0$, $w_0\in\mathbf C^d$, and $s\geq0$. With the product topology on $\mathbf C^d$, the closed polydisc
$$Q_s=\{w\in\mathbf C^d:|w_j-w_{0j}|\leq s\text{ for every }1\leq j\leq d\}$$
is compact. Moreover, if $X$ is any topological space and $K\subseteq X$ is compact, then $K\times Q_s$ is compact in $X\times\mathbf C^d$. Compact means every open cover admits a finite subcover, and subsets carry their subspace topologies [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Empty $K$ and $d=0$ are allowed; for $d=0$ the polydisc is a singleton.
